triggers: a kernel on AMD MI308X (CDNA3 / gfx942) risks the '31. `sched_dsrd(2) + sched_mfma(2)` over-constrains compiler when mask VALU needs MFMA latency bubbles' trap

payload.goal: Avoid a known trap on AMD MI308X (CDNA3 / gfx942): 31. `sched_dsrd(2) + sched_mfma(2)` over-constrains compiler when mask VALU needs MFMA latency bubbles

problem.statement: Pitfalls: FlyDSL Flash Attention on MI308X (gfx942) -- 31. `sched_dsrd(2) + sched_mfma(2)` over-constrains compiler when mask VALU needs MFMA latency bubbles

payload.attempted: The causal+GQA variant uses `sched_dsrd(2) + sched_mfma(2)` at the GEMM1 start to hint the compiler to interleave 2 ds_reads with 2 MFMAs. "This should also work for the mask variant — the GEMM1 structure is the same."
payload.lesson: Scheduling hints that are optimal for one kernel variant may be harmful for another. When adding new compute work (mask VALU) that can fill MFMA latency bubbles, prefer `sched_barrier(0)` (unconstrained) over `sched_dsrd/sched_mfma` (semi-constrained). The key insight is that MFMA has 64-cycle pipeline latency where other work can execute for free — hints that prevent this interleaving leave performance on the table.

established_fact.mechanism: `sched_dsrd(N) + sched_mfma(N)` are soft scheduling hints that guide the compiler to interleave N ds_reads with N MFMAs. This works well for the causal variant where the only non-MFMA work is K/V LDS reads. But with bit-packed mask, there are additional VALU instructions (AND/CMP/CNDMASK/AddF per element) that can productively fill MFMA's 64-cycle pipeline latency bubbles. The dsrd/mfma hints prevent the compiler from scheduling mask VALU during MFMA stalls, leaving cycles wasted. `sched_barrier(0)` resets the scheduling state entirely, giving the compiler full freedom to interleave mask VALU with MFMA.

payload.observed: Replacing `sched_dsrd(2) + sched_mfma(2)` with `sched_barrier(0)` at GEMM1 start gave +1.8% (49.8 → 50.6 TFLOPS) on the bit-packed mask variant.
